name: Neuronal Tumor

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Neuronal Tumors

criteria.description: Presence of neuronal differentiation confirmed by immunohistochemistry (e.g., synaptophysin, NeuN positivity)
MRI showing well-demarcated lesion with characteristic signal intensities on T1 and T2 weighted images
Neurological symptoms consistent with tumor location such as seizures or focal neurological deficits

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of neuronal differentiation plus compatible neuroimaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory

searchTerms: seizures starting in one area of brain
gradual worsening of localized neurological problems
progressive weakness or numbness in one area
pain in head near tumor site

common.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting due to increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: feeling sick from increased brain pressure
weakness on one side of body
fluid buildup in brain from tumor blockage
brain swelling due to blocked fluid flow
water on the brain caused by tumor

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction due to hypothalamic involvement
searchTerms: hormone problems from brain area damage
endocrine issues due to hypothalamus involvement
hormonal imbalance caused by brain tumor

laboratory: CSF analysis typically normal but may show mild protein elevation
imaging: MRI demonstrating well-circumscribed lesion with mixed signal intensities
Contrast enhancement variable, often mild to moderate
genetic: Molecular alterations such as BRAF mutations may be present in some neuronal tumors
other: Histopathology showing neuronal differentiation with immunohistochemical markers (synaptophysin, NeuN)

distinguishingFeatures: Glial cell origin vs neuronal differentiation
Different immunohistochemical profile (GFAP positive in gliomas)

redFlags: New onset of focal seizures in adult
Signs of increased intracranial pressure such as persistent vomiting and papilledema
references: Louis DN et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition, 2021.
Orphanet Report on Neuronal Tumors, ORPHA:251924.
Kleihues P, Cavenee WK. Pathology and Genetics of Tumors of the Nervous System. IARC Press, 2000.
